notes.text:
**Genesis 27:24** — וַיֹּאמֶר אַתָּה זֶה בְּנִי עֵשָׂו וַיֹּאמֶר אָנִי. Isaac asks once more, "Are you really my son Esau?" and Jacob answers with the single word "I."
The whole os turns on how this one-word answer could be true. *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: לֹא אָמַר אֲנִי עֵשָׂו אֶלָּא אָנִי
notes.text:
**Rashi on Genesis 27:24** — וַיֹּאמֶר אָנִי: לֹא אָמַר אֲנִי עֵשָׂו אֶלָּא אָנִי. Rashi notes that Jacob avoided saying "I am Esau" and said only "I."
Rav Tzadok accepts Rashi's observation but argues it does not yet remove the difficulty, since "I" in reply to the question still implies "I am Esau." *Mafteach: missing*

**Rashi on Genesis 27:19** — אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו בְּכֹרֶךָ: אָנֹכִי הַמֵּבִיא לְךָ וְעֵשָׂו הוּא בְּכוֹרֶךָ. Rashi splits Jacob's first statement in two: "I am the one bringing you [the food], and Esau is your firstborn."
Rav Tzadok's point is that this reading works for verse 19 but cannot be applied to the bare "I" of verse 24. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Parshat Shekalim 3** (Rav Tzadok) — states the same rule, "לשון זה מורה שהדבר מפורש לנגד עיניו שיוכל להראות באצבע," with the same proof from Megillah 15b (Haman's treasures engraved on his heart); there he applies it to "זה אלהיך" at the Golden Calf and to "זה יתנו" of the half-shekel, so "zeh" also marks what is engraved in the heart. *checked*

**Megillah 15b** (on **Esther 5:13**) — "וְכׇל זֶה אֵינֶנּוּ שֹׁוֶה לִי" — מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכׇּל גְּנָזָיו שֶׁל אוֹתוֹ רָשָׁע חֲקוּקִין עַל לִבּוֹ. The Gemara reads Haman's "all this is worth nothing to me" as showing that he carried an inventory of all his treasures engraved on his heart.
Rav Tzadok takes from this that "zeh" ("this") is said only of something present and pointable, so Isaac's "Are you *this* one" was spoken while touching Jacob. *Mafteach: found*

**Micah 7:20** (unnamed) — תִּתֵּן אֱמֶת לְיַעֲקֹב חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם. "You will give truth to Jacob, kindness to Abraham": the source for truth as Jacob's defining attribute, which Rav Tzadok assumes here without quoting. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Vayeshev 8** (Rav Tzadok) — opens with the same question, "שיעקב אע"ה שמדתו אמת יוכל לצאת מפיו דבר שאינו אמת," about "טרוף טורף יוסף," and answers that Jacob's words were true on a deeper level (the "evil beast" is the serpent's flaw of lashon hara). *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Toldot 6** (Rav Tzadok) — continues this os: Jacob's truth includes the wisdom to deal cunningly with a deceiver ("ועם עקש תתפל"), and it refers back here: "וענין שאכילתו שלמים הוא מה שאמר ליצחק אני וכמו שאמרנו." *checked*

**Bamidbar Rabbah 16:10; Midrash Tanchuma, Shelach 6** — שְׁמוֹתֵיהֶם נָאִים וּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם כְּעוּרִים, זֶה יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְעֵשָׂו, יִשְׁמָעֵאל, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֵל, עֵשָׂו, עוֹשֶׂה רְצוֹן עוֹשָׂיו. Among those whose names are fine but whose deeds are ugly are Ishmael ("God hears") and Esau ("one who does his Maker's will").
The original print reads "במ"ר ומד"ת שלח," that is, Bamidbar Rabbah and Tanchuma Shelach (both on the spies' names); the interlinear's "Bereishit Rabbah 65" expands the abbreviation wrongly. Bereishit Rabbah 71:3 has a similar list but explains Esau's name differently ("שְׁמוֹ עֵשָׂו וְאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה"), not in the words quoted here. *Mafteach: found*

notes.anchor: יִצְחָק נִתְעַטֵּר בְּאַבְרָהָם וְאַבְרָהָם נִתְעַטֵּר בְּיִצְחָק
notes.text:
**Midrash Tanchuma, Toldot 4** — אֲבָל יִצְחָק נִתְעַטֵּר בְּאַבְרָהָם, וְאַבְרָהָם נִתְעַטֵּר בְּיִצְחָק. After proving that Jacob was saved by Abraham's merit ("לוּלֵי אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וּפַחַד יִצְחָק"), the Midrash concludes that Isaac was crowned through Abraham and Abraham through Isaac.
"כמו שאמרנו" refers to Toldot 1, where Rav Tzadok reads the "crowns" as each patriarch taking on the other's attribute. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: תנחומא ד, no source key)*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 1:3–4** (Rav Tzadok) — the explanation this os depends on: Abraham was "crowned" by Isaac's fear at the Akeidah ("עתה ידעתי כי ירא אלהים אתה") and Isaac by Abraham's love; love yields the positive commandments and fear the negative ones, the two crowns of Sinai. It also answers "אנכי עשו בכורך" another way: by wearing Esau's garments Jacob drew out the holy sparks in Esau, so "what found favor in your eyes in Esau is already in my hand." *checked*

**Genesis 31:42** (unnamed) — לוּלֵי אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי אֱלֹהֵי אַבְרָהָם וּפַחַד יִצְחָק הָיָה לִי. Jacob calls God "the Fear of Isaac": the scriptural name for Isaac's attribute of awe, and the verse the Tanchuma itself quotes. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.anchor: כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה
notes.text:
**Genesis 22:12** — כִּי עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה וְלֹא חָשַׂכְתָּ אֶת בִּנְךָ אֶת יְחִידְךָ מִמֶּנִּי. At the Akeidah the angel declares that Abraham is now known to fear God.
Rav Tzadok reads it as the moment Abraham, the man of love, was completed by Isaac's fear. *Mafteach: found*

**Peri Tzadik, Chayei Sara 7** — "שעסק אברהם אבינו ע"ה היה השתדלות במ"ע. שמדתו היה אהבה ... ומדת יצחק הפחד והיראה ומזה בא השמירה במל"ת." There Rav Tzadok bases the division (Abraham's love giving zeal in positive commandments, Isaac's fear giving care over prohibitions) on Yerushalmi Berakhot (cited in Tosafot Sotah 22b) and Chullin 16a, "קרא זריזותיה דאברהם." *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 22:18** — וְהִתְבָּרְכוּ בְזַרְעֲךָ כֹּל גּוֹיֵי הָאָרֶץ עֵקֶב אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַעְתָּ בְּקֹלִי. The blessing after the Akeidah is given "because you listened to My voice."
Rav Tzadok links "you listened" (shamata) to the crown of "nishma": restraint before God's word, the quality Abraham gained from Isaac. *Mafteach: found*

**Exodus 24:7; Shabbat 88a** (unnamed) — בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁהִקְדִּימוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל ״נַעֲשֶׂה״ לְ״נִשְׁמָע״ ... לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל קָשְׁרוּ לוֹ שְׁנֵי כְתָרִים, אֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד ״נַעֲשֶׂה״ וְאֶחָד כְּנֶגֶד ״נִשְׁמָע״. When Israel put "we will do" before "we will hear," each Jew received two crowns, one for each word.
Rav Tzadok maps the two crowns onto the patriarchs: "na'aseh" is Abraham's active zeal, "nishma" is Isaac's careful listening. *Mafteach: missing*

**Peri Tzadik, Toldot 1:3–4** — "ונתעטרו בב' כתרים שהם משורש מ"ע ומצות ל"ת אנכי ולא יהי'." Earlier in this parashah Rav Tzadok ties the two Sinai crowns to "Anochi" (root of the positive commandments, Abraham) and "Lo yihyeh" (root of the prohibitions, Isaac). *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 25:27** (unnamed) — וַיְהִי עֵשָׂו אִישׁ יֹדֵעַ צַיִד אִישׁ שָׂדֶה וְיַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּם יֹשֵׁב אֹהָלִים. Esau is the man of the field and Jacob the wholesome man who stays in the tents.
Rav Tzadok reads Isaac's view through this verse: Jacob's place was the tent of Torah and prayer, Esau's the field of practical deeds. *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 27:20** — וַיֹּאמֶר יִצְחָק אֶל בְּנוֹ מַה זֶּה מִהַרְתָּ לִמְצֹא בְּנִי וַיֹּאמֶר כִּי הִקְרָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְפָנָי. Asked how he found game so quickly, Jacob answers that "Hashem your God" arranged it for him. *Mafteach: found*

**Bereshit Rabbah 65:19** — בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַר כִּי הִקְרָה ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ לְפָנָי, אָמַר יִצְחָק יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁאֵין עֵשָׂו מַזְכִּיר שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, זֶה מַזְכִּיר, אֵין זֶה עֵשָׂו אֶלָּא יַעֲקֹב. When God's Name was mentioned, Isaac concluded that the speaker could not be Esau, who did not speak of God.
Rav Tzadok explains why Isaac, who thought well of Esau, would reason this way: the Names spoken belonged to Torah and prayer, which Isaac counted as Jacob's field. *Mafteach: missing*

**Ramban on Genesis 27:21** — וַאֲנִי תָּמֵהַּ כִּי לֹא הָיָה עֵשָׂו רָשָׁע בְּעֵינֵי אָבִיו. Ramban asks how Isaac could think Esau never mentioned God when Esau was not wicked in his eyes. Ramban suggests Isaac saw the omission as Esau's reverence: he avoided the Name for fear of saying it in an impure place.
Rav Tzadok answers differently: Isaac thought Esau's service was deeds, not the Names of Torah and prayer. *Mafteach: missing*

**Zohar II 60a (Beshalach)** — וְאוֹלִיפְנָא דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִקְרֵי, וְאֵין מַיִם אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, וְאֵין תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא. On Israel finding no water in the wilderness, the Zohar teaches that the Holy One is called Torah, so lacking water meant lacking Him.
Rav Tzadok uses it to tie the Name Havayah to Torah. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 21a** (on **Deuteronomy 32:3**) — מִנַּיִן לְבִרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה לְפָנֶיהָ מִן הַתּוֹרָה — שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי שֵׁם ה׳ אֶקְרָא הָבוּ גֹדֶל לֵאלֹהֵינוּ״. The blessing before Torah study is derived from "When I call the Name of Hashem."
Torah reading counts as "calling the Name," which shows that the Name Havayah stands for Torah. *Mafteach: found*

**Berakhot 6a** (on **Exodus 20:21**) — וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ אֶחָד שֶׁיּוֹשֵׁב וְעוֹסֵק בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁשְּׁכִינָה עִמּוֹ — שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בְּכָל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי אָבוֹא אֵלֶיךָ וּבֵרַכְתִּיךָ״. The Divine Presence rests even on one person who sits and studies Torah, from "in every place where I cause My Name to be mentioned."
In the verse, "mentioning My Name" means Torah study, so the Name again stands for Torah. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 3:2** (Rav Tzadok) — joins the same two derashot ("ושמי נקרא ד"ת כמו שנדרש (שם כא.) לברכת התורה ... " and Berakhot 6a on "בכל המקום אשר אזכיר את שמי") to explain why blessings followed Jacob's meal; it adds that the verse is said of the altar, so the meal and Torah study both work like offerings. *checked*

**Zohar I 137b (Toldot)** — תָּא חֲזֵי, אַבְרָהָם לָא צַלֵּי קַמֵּי קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא דְּיִתֵּן לֵיהּ בְּנִין, אַף עַל גַּב דְּשָׂרָה עֲקָרָה הֲוַת ... אֲבָל יִצְחָק צַלֵּי עַל אִתְּתֵיהּ. Abraham never prayed for children although Sarah was barren; his words "You have given me no seed" were talk before his Master, not prayer. Isaac did pray for his wife.
This is the basis for linking prayer with Isaac's attribute. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar I 135b; correct: Zohar I 137b)*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Vayera 5** (Rav Tzadok) — cites the same Zohar with the same folio, "(תולדות קלז ב) שלא מצינו שהתפלל על בנים ורק ביצחק כ' ויעתר יצחק," and the same claim that Abraham's first prayer was for Sodom, for others and not himself; it also has the same reading of "הקל קול יעקב" as "קל ה' ... קול ו'," and adds that the Sodom prayer saved Lot, from whom David, the root of prayer, descends. *checked*

**Berakhot 6b** (on **Genesis 19:27**) — ״וַיַּשְׁכֵּם אַבְרָהָם בַּבֹּקֶר אֶל הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר עָמַד שָׁם״, וְאֵין ״עֲמִידָה״ אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיַּעֲמֹד פִּינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּל״. Abraham returned to "the place where he had stood," and "standing" means prayer. Berakhot 26b repeats this in its account of Abraham instituting Shacharit.
The original reads "ברכות שם ע"ב," that is, 6b; the interlinear leaves out the side of the folio. *Mafteach: found*

**Sanhedrin 44a** (on **Psalms 106:30**) — ״וַיַּעֲמֹד פִּינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּל״ ... ״וַיִּתְפַּלֵּל״ לֹא נֶאֱמַר אֶלָּא ״וַיְפַלֵּל״, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁעָשָׂה פְּלִילוּת עִם קוֹנוֹ. The verse uses "vayefalel," not "vayitpalel," to teach that Pinchas argued a case with his Maker.
Rav Tzadok uses it to explain "standing" prayer: an advocate who argues for others, as Abraham did for Sodom, with no personal stake. *Mafteach: found*

**Psalms 102:1; Berakhot 26b** (unnamed) — יִצְחָק תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת מִנְחָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיֵּצֵא יִצְחָק לָשׂוּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶה לִפְנוֹת עָרֶב״, וְאֵין ״שִׂיחָה״ אֶלָּא תְּפִלָּה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״תְּפִלָּה לְעָנִי כִי יַעֲטֹף וְלִפְנֵי ה׳ יִשְׁפֹּךְ שִׂיחוֹ״. Isaac's prayer is called "sichah," proved from the poor man who "pours out his speech."
Rav Tzadok takes the verse's poor man to mean that sichah is prayer about one's own distress, as against Abraham's prayer for others. *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 27:22** — הַקֹּל קוֹל יַעֲקֹב וְהַיָּדַיִם יְדֵי עֵשָׂו. The first "kol" is written without a vav (קֹל), the second in full (קוֹל).
Rav Tzadok reads the two spellings as the two "voices" Isaac heard in Jacob's "Hashem your God": prayer and Torah. *Mafteach: found*

**Psalms 51:17** — אֲדֹנָי שְׂפָתַי תִּפְתָּח וּפִי יַגִּיד תְּהִלָּתֶךָ. The verse said before the Amidah opens with the Name Adonai, so prayer belongs to that Name. The defective "קל" has the numerical value of the Name's final heh. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Psalms 51:15; correct: Psalms 51:17)*

**Zohar III 2a (Vayikra)** — וּנְתַתֶּם לִי אוֹת אֱמֶת, דָּא אָת ו', דְּדָא אִקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת. The Zohar reads Rahab's request for "a true sign" as the letter vav, which is called "the letter of truth." *Mafteach: found*

**Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 3:8** (on **Proverbs 23:23**; unnamed) — וְאֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תוֹרָה. הֵיךְ מַה דְאַתְּ אָמַר אֱמֶת קְנֵה וְאַל תִּמְכּוֹר. "Truth" means Torah, as in "Buy truth and do not sell it." The same teaching appears in Eikhah Rabbah, Petichta 2.
This closes the chain: the full "קוֹל" with vav is truth, and truth is Torah. *Mafteach: missing*

**Genesis 27:19** — וַיֹּאמֶר יַעֲקֹב אֶל אָבִיו אָנֹכִי עֵשָׂו בְּכֹרֶךָ עָשִׂיתִי כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבַּרְתָּ אֵלָי. Jacob's first self-identification to Isaac.
Rav Tzadok's answer: "Esau" here means what the name means, "doer of his Maker's will," and Jacob truly was that. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Ben Porat Yosef, Toldot 86** (Chassidus) — also holds that Jacob told the plain truth in "I am Esau your firstborn," and also ties "your firstborn" to the fact that the service belonged to the firstborn; for him Jacob turned Esau, the "matter," into "form," which is the firstborn.
וז"ש אנכי עשו בכורך, כי אמת אמר, אנכי עשיתי מן עשו שהוא חומר עשיתי אותו צורה שהוא בכורך

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Degel Machaneh Ephraim, Toldot 14** (Chassidus) — asks the same question (how could Jacob, the attribute of truth, say something false) and calls Rashi's answer forced; he solves it by reading "Anochi" as the whole Torah contained in that word, which Jacob is.
ותמהו כאן כל המפרשי' איך יעקב שהוא מדת אמת יוציא דבר שקר מפיו

**Mishnah Zevachim 14:4; Rashi on Genesis 25:31** (unnamed) — עַד שֶׁלֹּא הוּקַם הַמִּשְׁכָּן, הָיוּ הַבָּמוֹת מֻתָּרוֹת, וַעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת. Before the Mishkan the sacrificial service belonged to the firstborn. Rashi applies this to the sale of the birthright: לְפִי שֶׁהָעֲבוֹדָה בַּבְּכוֹרוֹת.
So "your firstborn" identifies the speaker as the one who brings offerings. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.text:
**Zohar I 142a (Toldot)** — תָּא חֲזֵי, יַעֲקֹב כָּל עוֹבָדוֹי הֲווּ לִשְׁמָא דְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא, וּבְגִין כָּךְ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הֲוָה עִמֵּיהּ תָּדִיר. All of Jacob's deeds were for the sake of the Holy One, so the Shechinah never left him.
On this basis Rav Tzadok calls Jacob, more than Esau, the "doer of his Maker's will." *Mafteach: found*

**Proverbs 13:25** (unnamed) — צַדִּיק אֹכֵל לְשֹׂבַע נַפְשׁוֹ וּבֶטֶן רְשָׁעִים תֶּחְסָר. "The righteous man eats to satisfy his soul": the eating of the righteous feeds the soul, which is why it can count as an offering. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels:** **Peri Tzadik, Toldot 3** (Rav Tzadok) — the "כמו שאמרנו": the meal of a Torah scholar is "כקרבן ממש" (Berakhot 10b, Yoma 71a, Ketubot 105b), and Jacob hinted in "כי הקרה" (Bereshit Rabbah 65:19, "אם לקורבנך המציא לך") that Isaac's eating was like offerings, even greater. *checked*
**Peri Tzadik, Toldot 6** (Rav Tzadok) — "וצדיק אוכל לשובע נפשו הוה אכילתו כקרבנות וכשלמים ... וענין שאכילתו שלמים הוא מה שאמר ליצחק אני וכמו שאמרנו": the next os uses the same verse and refers to this os's reading of "אני." *checked*

**Parallels:** **Sod Yesharim, Sukkot 57** (Ishbitz–Radzin) — also holds that "באמת לא היה נמצא ביעקב אבינו שום לשון רמיה בזה שהיה אומר אנכי עשו בכורך," but on other grounds: God created Esau only so that honor of Heaven would come out of him into Israel, so Jacob contains Esau and spoke "באמת לאמיתו"; he reads this through the Zohar's "הצילה נפשי משפת שקר" (Toldot 142b). *checked*

**Bereshit Rabbah 65:22** (on **Genesis 27:27**) — דָּבָר אַחֵר, וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו וַיְבָרֲכֵהוּ, כְּגוֹן יוֹסֵף מְשִׁיתָא וְיָקוּם אִישׁ צְרוֹרוֹת. Isaac smelled in Jacob's garments people like Yosef Meshita and Yakum of Tzeror, two traitors who in the end gave their lives in repentance.
For Rav Tzadok these are the "fragrance" Isaac sensed: Jacob's own descendants who strayed but still give off a good scent. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **Yismach Moshe, Toldot 21** (Chassidus) — joins the same two teachings, Bereshit Rabbah 65:22 (Yosef Meshita and Yakum) and Sanhedrin 37a ("בוגדיו"), and explains them by levels within Klal Yisrael: before their repentance these men were only the "garment" of Jacob, so their scent is the scent of his garments.
והיינו בגדיו שהן בחינת הלבוש של יעקב והבן

**Sanhedrin 37a** — רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר: מֵהָכָא, ״וַיָּרַח אֶת רֵיחַ בְּגָדָיו״. אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״בְּגָדָיו״ אֶלָּא ״בּוֹגְדָיו״. Read "his garments" as "his betrayers": even Israel's betrayers give off a fragrance. *Mafteach: found*

**Sanhedrin 37a** (on **Song of Songs 4:3**) — ״כְּפֶלַח הָרִמּוֹן רַקָּתֵךְ״ – אֲפִילּוּ רֵיקָנִין שֶׁבָּךְ מְלֵאִין מִצְוֹת כְּרִמּוֹן. Even the "empty" ones among Israel are as full of mitzvot as a pomegranate. Resh Lakish says this on the same line of the Gemara as Rabbi Zeira's "bogedav," which is why Rav Tzadok writes "כמש"ש."
The wording "פושעי ישראל" matches Eruvin 19a (similar sayings at Berakhot 57a and Megillah 6a), but the passage he points to is Sanhedrin 37a. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Berakhot 57a, Eruvin 19a, Megillah 6a; correct: Sanhedrin 37a)*
